// Package subject is the ifacereturn fixture: one declaration per shape the
// analyzer must report or stay silent about.
//
// It is held as .go.txt and materialized into a temporary GOPATH by the test,
// for the reason the house-code-style evals hold their fixtures the same way:
// a fixture full of deliberate violations must not join the tracked Go corpus,
// where the blocking CS-1/CS-2/CS-8 gate, the dupl reuse gate and the census
// would all read it as real code.
package subject

import (
	"io"

	"thirdparty"
)

// IStore is a repository-owned interface, in the shape CS-1 names.
type IStore interface {
	Get(key string) string
}

type memoryStore struct{}

// Get implements IStore.
func (memoryStore) Get(key string) string { return key }

// NewStore returns a repository-owned interface: the founding CS-8 shape.
func NewStore() IStore { return memoryStore{} } // want "NewStore returns the interface subject.IStore"

// OpenReader returns a standard-library interface, which the lexical lane
// cannot see because the corpus declares no interface named Reader.
func OpenReader(name string) io.Reader { return nil } // want "OpenReader returns the interface io.Reader"

// OpenSink returns a third-party interface, invisible to the lexical lane for
// the same reason.
func OpenSink(name string) thirdparty.Sink { return nil } // want "OpenSink returns the interface thirdparty.Sink"

// Validate returns only error, the rule's single structural exemption.
func Validate(value string) error { return nil }

// Load returns an interface and an error: exactly one finding, and it says
// which result it means.
func Load(key string) (IStore, error) { return memoryStore{}, nil } // want "Load returns the interface subject.IStore .result 1 of 2."

// Decode returns any, which is an interface however it is spelled.
func Decode(raw []byte) any { return nil } // want "Decode returns the interface any"

// NewMemoryStore returns a concrete value: silent.
func NewMemoryStore() memoryStore { return memoryStore{} }

// NewMemoryStorePointer returns a concrete pointer: silent.
func NewMemoryStorePointer() *memoryStore { return nil }

// AllStores returns a slice of interfaces. A caller that receives the slice
// receives the interfaces, so the container is not a boundary.
func AllStores() []IStore { return nil } // want "AllStores returns the interface subject.IStore"

// View is a struct that carries an interface. A caller that receives one
// receives the IStore inside it, which is the 2026-09-03 amendment.
type View struct {
	Store IStore
	Name  string
}

// Inner nests a View, so the reported path has to name both hops.
type Inner struct {
	View View
}

// Recursive is the cycle guard's fixture: a type that reaches itself. Without
// the visited set the walk would not terminate; with it, the interface below
// is reported exactly once.
type Recursive struct {
	Next  *Recursive
	Store IStore
}

// NewView returns a struct carrying an interface: one finding, naming the way
// through.
func NewView() View { return View{} } // want "NewView returns View.Store, which is the interface subject.IStore"

// NewViews returns a slice of them, which is the same handover in a container.
func NewViews() []View { return nil } // want "NewViews returns View.Store, which is the interface subject.IStore"

// NewInner is two hops, and the path says so.
func NewInner() *Inner { return nil } // want "NewInner returns Inner.View.Store, which is the interface subject.IStore"

// NewRecursive terminates, and reports the one interface once.
func NewRecursive() *Recursive { return nil } // want "NewRecursive returns Recursive.Store, which is the interface subject.IStore"

// Options carries a callback rather than an implementation. A func-typed field
// is not followed: a callback is a contract the caller supplies or invokes,
// not an implementation handed over.
type Options struct {
	Authenticate func() IStore
}

// NewOptions is silent for that reason.
func NewOptions() Options { return Options{} }

// Plain carries no interface at all: silent.
type Plain struct{ Name string }

// NewPlain returns it.
func NewPlain() Plain { return Plain{} }

// Zero returns the caller's own type parameter. types.IsInterface reports true
// for a type parameter — its underlying type is its constraint — so silence
// here is the analyzer's TypeParam guard doing its job.
func Zero[Value any]() Value {
	var zero Value
	return zero
}

// Registry exercises method position, which the lexical lane declines by scope.
type Registry struct{}

// Store returns a repository-owned interface from a value receiver.
func (Registry) Store() IStore { return memoryStore{} } // want ".Registry..Store returns the interface subject.IStore"

// Reader returns a standard-library interface from a pointer receiver.
func (registry *Registry) Reader() io.Reader { return nil } // want ".\\*Registry..Reader returns the interface io.Reader"

// Close returns error from method position: still exempt.
func (registry *Registry) Close() error { return nil }
